agent.problem: David is named as the psalm's author, but he is not simply identified as a person when he first appears, such as by giving his role in Israel.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

human.problem: Papa Dorin calls verse 10 'the line this psalm is named for.' The psalm's own heading in the text is 'A Psalm of David.' 'Teach Me to Do Your Will' is the passage title the lesson uses. That may count as talking about how lessons are made, and it may not be true of the psalm itself.
human.question: May Papa Dorin refer to the passage title, for example by saying the psalm is 'named for' a line, or should he only refer to headings that appear in the BSB text itself?

human.problem: All three true or false cards (cards 10, 14 and 17) have True as the right answer. Each one restates the verse almost word for word. A baker who notices this can answer True every time without thinking about the passage.
human.question: Should true or false cards in a stop mix True and False right answers, or avoid near-verbatim true statements, so the type doesn't become a free pick? The 'No formula' rule covers the order of question types, but not which answer is right.
